    codex: add exact failed-turn continuation and context reads
    
    Expose cold latest-turn failure metadata and exact native execution context
    without guessing from current defaults. The context projection validates
    Codex 0.163.0 rollout identities and supported policy shapes while keeping
    prompts, instructions and application authority out of the returned value.
    
    Continue an exact failed turn only while its thread is already loaded and
    quiescent, with raw idle or systemError status and an exact terminal turn.
    Preserve original options and reconcile durable receipts before fresh
    admission checks. An atomic submitting claim prevents competing clients
    from dispatching the same identity twice. This path never resumes, steers
    or writes policy; applications retain the shared admission and authority
    fences, including the native protocol's lack of compare-and-start.
    
    Keep the schema-3 submission ledger and existing send behavior compatible.

    conversation: expose optional application-owned retry controls
    
    Add an optional retry provider and capability without changing the required
    App Server client interface. Resolve each opaque conversation through the
    application and keep preference/cancel writes behind existing origin,
    payload and shared mutation-lock checks. The provider retains durable
    policy, authority and scheduling.
    
    Offer an opt-in Auto retry checkbox, server-relative countdown, quota
    status and Cancel retry control. Read authoritative state after reload,
    focus and uncertain writes; the browser never starts a continuation.
    Cancellation preserves the preference and cannot retract dispatched work.
    Existing embeddings keep their current interface with retry controls off.

    codex: verify failed-turn retries against a private native fixture
    
    Share the existing recovery fixture's private home, native process and
    loopback Responses provider with a focused failed-turn contract test.
    Synthetic failure events exercise terminal classification and retained
    command output without real keys or policy-triggering requests.
    
    Check nonempty continuation settings, native queue execution context and
    recreated-client recovery after a dropped accepted reply. A transparent
    protocol proxy also forces competing native work after the final preflight,
    so native busy-turn behavior remains an explicit deployment gate rather
    than an assumption made from fake transport tests.

    codex: expose exact prepared-send observation proofs
    
    Distinguish an exact unsubmitted preparation from accepted, submitting or
    queue-owned work without changing SendAttempted semantics. Applications can
    exclude that one preparation from submission observation while retaining
    ordinary checks for every other attempt and queue deletion.
    
    Keep the original identity, options, steering flag and ledger unchanged.
    The proof does not authorize dispatch or replace application admission
    fences. Existing native and durable state formats remain compatible.

    conversation: add optional retry activity notices and actions
    
    Expose safe retry-chain observations through an optional provider and token-only
    Now and Stop routes. Resolve trusted conversation authority for every call and
    retain the existing origin, payload and mutation-lock boundaries. Keep legacy
    retry providers and the required App Server client interface unchanged.
    
    Offer a reusable footer notice with confirmed starts, uncertain submissions,
    server-relative countdowns and honest elapsed-time quality through execution
    and frozen results. Dismiss each exact conversation and chain locally, including
    when browser storage is unavailable. Coalesce observations and reconcile lost
    action responses by reading; the browser never dispatches a continuation.
    
    Applications own scheduling, durable policy, cancellation and transcript scroll
    behavior. Native protocols and submission formats are unchanged.
